# New Snack Product Line — Refined Proposal, Offered for the Group's Alignment

With respect to the earlier draft: it offered a creative and culturally grounded foundation, and we have sought to build upon it rather than replace it. In reviewing it together, we felt a few areas might benefit from additional commercial scaffolding before the work is presented upward. We humbly offer the refined version below for the team's consideration.

## 1. First, a Quiet Word on the Target Market

The brief understandably leaves the destination unspecified. Rather than proceed on a single assumption, we thought it prudent to offer a short selection framework — so the group may align on the market — and then develop one market in depth as a concrete working basis.

| Criterion | Japan | Mexico | Germany |
|---|---|---|---|
| Market size & growth | Large, mature; premium and health segments growing | Large, youthful, growing | Large, stable; private-label heavy |
| Fit with typical snack capabilities | High, if rice/texture formats are feasible | High (corn, chili formats) | Medium |
| Competitive intensity | Very high | High | High |
| Route-to-market barriers | High (distributor-mediated) | Medium | Medium (discounter gatekeepers) |
| Premium headroom | High | Medium | Medium-low |

For concreteness, we have developed **Japan** below. Should leadership already hold a different market in mind, we would gratefully receive that guidance — the framework transfers readily, and we would be glad to redevelop the detail accordingly.

## 2. Market Context (Directional — to Be Validated)

- Japan's broader packaged confectionery/snack market exceeds ¥3 trillion, with savory snacks on the order of ¥1.2–1.4 trillion. Overall growth is modest; **premium, health-positioned, and adult evening-snack (*otsumami*) segments are outpacing the category**.
- Over 55,000 convenience stores (*konbini*) dominate impulse snacking — but SKUs churn weekly, and delisting follows quickly if velocity disappoints.
- Recovering inbound tourism is reviving gift (*omiyage*) demand.
- We would respectfully suggest commissioning syndicated data (e.g., Intage, Fuji Keizai) before any gate decision; the figures above are directional only.

## 3. Competitive Snapshot — Where We Might Quietly Fit

- **Mass salty snacks** are dominated by Calbee (potato snacks), Kameda Seika (rice crackers), and Glico/Lotte (sticks, pretzels), all with locked distribution and the ability to fast-follow a flavor within a season.
- **Konbini private labels** compete aggressively on price and rotate rapidly.
- **Implication:** we will not win on flavor novelty alone — flavors are copied within months. More defensible space lies in (a) **format and texture innovation** requiring process capability, (b) a **coherent premium platform** with disciplined seasonal cadence, and (c) the **fragmented adult otsumami segment**, which lacks a strong branded platform.

## 4. The Product Line — "Shun" (旬) Platform, Refined

Our proposed resolution of the novelty/familiarity tension: **familiar flavors (low trial barrier) delivered through novel formats and textures (defensible differentiation).**

**Line A — Craft Otsumami (proposed lead).** Savory, premium, built for evening drinks at home — an occasion that has held its post-pandemic gains. Yuzu-kosho rice crackers; smoked-shoyu almonds wrapped in nori; sansho-dusted broad beans. Differentiation through sourcing stories and resealable premium pouches, not flavor alone. (Mentaiko popcorn is a crowded SKU; we would gently suggest differentiating on ingredient provenance or deprioritizing it.)

**Line B — Saku-Mochi (hero, subject to a technical gate).** Crispy roasted-rice shell around a chewy mochi center — the line's genuine differentiator, and also its highest technical risk. Mochi hardens through starch retrogradation; a shelf-stable crispy-chewy format over a six-month life is a real formulation challenge. We propose partnering with an established mochi co-manufacturer and requiring a **shelf-life validation gate** (accelerated testing, e.g., texture retention under 40°C/75%RH conditions) before any launch commitment.

**Line C — Oyatsu at Three (supporting).** Individually wrapped, gently sweet desk-drawer items: hojicha shortbread thins, glazed satsumaimo chips, okara-kinako cookies. Sweetness should be set by **sensory benchmarking against local category leaders** rather than an assumed percentage reduction.

**Line D — Omiyage Regional Collection (restructured, or respectfully deferred).** The earlier concept carries a quiet provenance risk: omiyage value rests on regional authenticity, and a single brand curating prefecture flavors without regional roots may read as inauthentic to the very consumers it courts. Two options for the group's reflection: (i) build **genuine regional co-manufacturing partnerships** — Hokkaido items made in Hokkaido with a local partner, co-branded — accepting a slower timeline; or (ii) defer omiyage in favor of an honestly positioned "regional journey" gift box sold online and in travel retail. We lean gently toward (i) as a Phase 3 development.

## 5. Occasion Mapping

| Occasion | Where/When | Best Fit | Format |
|---|---|---|---|
| Konbini impulse | Commute, lunch | Saku-Mochi singles (post-gate) | Small pouch, ¥140–180 |
| 3pm oyatsu | Office desk | Oyatsu line | Individually wrapped share box |
| Evening drinks | Home, post-work | Craft Otsumami | Resealable premium pouch |
| Gifting | Travel, seasonal | Regional Collection (Phase 3) | Co-branded gift box |
| Seasonal events | Hanami, matsuri | Limited editions | Share packs |

## 6. Route to Market — A Staged Path

May we be candid on one point: national konbini placement is the hardest problem in this plan, not a tactic. It requires entrenched wholesaler relationships and proven velocity, and shelf space is effectively earned, never assumed. We therefore propose:

- **Phase 0:** Online-first (Amazon Japan, Rakuten) plus *depachika* (department-store food hall) pop-ups — a premium stage, direct consumer data, low listing barriers.
- **Phase 1:** Selective retail — premium grocers (e.g., Seijo Ishii) or a regional konbini cluster via an established national wholesaler — to demonstrate sell-through.
- **Phase 2:** National konbini only with velocity data in hand, entered through a distributor already serving the chains. E-commerce remains the stable base throughout.

## 7. Regulatory & Operational Notes (for Awareness)

- **Food Labeling Act:** mandatory labeling of eight specified allergens (wheat, egg, milk, peanut, buckwheat, shrimp, crab, walnut), plus additive and ingredient-origin disclosure. Early engagement of local regulatory counsel is advisable.
- **Local co-manufacturing over import** is recommended — for freshness, tariff and logistics economics, yen exposure, consumer trust in domestic production, and to enable the regional partnership strategy.
- **Margin structure:** wholesaler and retail layers mean shelf price must carry roughly 2.5–3× ex-works cost (directional). Premium positioning is therefore not optional; it is structural.

## 8. Risk Register

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mochi shelf-life failure | Medium-high | High | Co-man partner; accelerated testing | Gate before Line B launch |
| Incumbent fast-follow on flavors | High | Medium | Compete on format/process + cadence | Continuous |
| Konbini delisting | Medium | High | Stage online/regional first; velocity thresholds | Phase 2 gate |
| Omiyage authenticity risk | Medium | Medium | Regional co-manufacturing or reposition | Phase 3 decision |
| Seasonal-edition fatigue | Medium | Medium | Disciplined cadence (4–6 drops/yr); evergreen core SKUs | Portfolio review |
| FX / input costs | Medium | Medium | Local sourcing; hedging | Finance review |
| Regulatory delay | Low-medium | Medium | Early local counsel | Phase 0 |

## 9. Phased Validation Plan (Targets Proposed for the Group's Calibration)

- **Phase 0 (months 0–4):** Central-location tests, n≈300–500; purchase intent at or above category benchmark; preference vs. local leaders; willingness-to-pay mapping. Kill criteria defined in advance.
- **Phase 1 (months 5–10):** Online + depachika + one regional retail cluster. Proposed thresholds: repeat purchase ≥25%; four-week sell-through ≥70%. Saku-Mochi shelf-life gate runs in parallel.
- **Phase 2 (months 11–18):** Expanded retail only if Phase 1 gates pass; national konbini pitch with data in hand.
- **Phase 3 (month 18+):** Omiyage via regional partnerships; seasonal cadence fully operational.

## 10. Our Humble Recommendation

If the team is aligned, we would respectfully propose: **lead with Craft Otsumami** — fastest to market, lowest technical risk, premium margin, fragmented competition — while **developing Saku-Mochi in parallel as the differentiating hero**, held firmly to its shelf-life gate. The Oyatsu line supports; omiyage is restructured around genuine regional partnerships for Phase 3.

This direction is offered for the group's alignment, and we would warmly welcome the perspectives of the commercial and R&D teams before the next milestone. Should leadership confirm a different target market, or prefer a different lead line, we would of course be glad to adjust and prepare accordingly.
